structure_save.summary: Saves a volume of the world as a structure template.
params: the name of the template, as `'mine:tower'`
optional: whether to save the entities too, `false` by default
structure_save.note: They are the **same templates as the vanilla structure block**, in the same place (`<world>/generated/<namespace>/structure/<name>.nbt`): what a script saves opens with a structure block, and the other way round.

signatures: structure_load(name, pos, rotation, mirror, with_entities, integrity, seed)
structure_load.summary: Places a structure template in the world.
params: the minimum corner of the result, whatever the rotation
optional: from `0` to `1`; below `1` it drops random blocks, like the structure block
optional: the seed of that randomness, to make a ruin repeatable
structure_load.returns: `bool` — whether it succeeded, `null` when the template does not exist.
examples:
// a repeatable ruin
structure.structure_load('mine:tower', pos, 0, 'none', true, 0.6, 12345);
structure_load.note: `pos` is always the minimum corner of the **result**: without this correction the same call with a different rotation would land somewhere else. It is also what makes `structure_load` and `structure_matches` reciprocal.

structure_matches.summary: Whether the region between two corners matches a template.
params: optional: the rotation to compare with
optional: the mirroring to compare with
structure_matches.returns: `bool` — whether it matches; `null` when the template does not exist, which is not the same as "does not match".
structure_matches.note: A region of a different size is discarded at once, without reading a single block. A template with several palettes matches when at least one of them does, and `structure_void` blocks do not count, as in vanilla.

structure_size.summary: The size of a template, taking a rotation into account.
structure_size.returns: `list` — `[x, y, z]`, `null` when the template does not exist.
examples:
// the far corner of a placement
structure.structure_size('mine:tower', 90);
